texts.facts: He was immediately rushed to Anshu Hospital, Palla, Faridabad, Haryana, for medical treatment. FIR under relevant provisions of law was registered at Police Station Sarai Khwaja, District Faridabad. Necessary investigation was undertaken. Driver of Swift Dezire Car was charge sheeted under relevant provisions of law. 2(b). It is stated that the injured was working as a helper and earning Rs. 20,000/- per month. WS filed on behalf of R-1/ driver. It is submitted that he was driving the offending vehicle with valid driving license issued by Sheikh Sarai Authority, NCT of Delhi. No WS/ Reply was filed on behalf of R-2. 3(c) In WS on behalf of R-3, the delay in registration of FIR was pointed out. It is also mentioned that the accident occurred on account of negligence and carelessness on the part of petitioner himself. It was conceded that the vehicle had a valid and effective insurance policy on the date of accident. Whether the injured suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident on 04.06.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR 55AB 9547 being driven by R-1, owned by R-2 and insured with R-3? Opp 2. 3. Relief. 5. Evidence: 5(a). Matter was then listed for evidence. Injured / Claimant Sh. Manoj Bhaskar tendered his evidentiary affidavit as Ex. PW1 / A. He relied upon following documents: Ex.PW1/1 - MLC Ex.PW1/2- Discharge Summaries Ex.PW1/3- Medical Prescriptions/ OPD Cards Ex.PW1/4- Medical Bills Ex.PW1/5- Copy of Aadhar Card and Pan Card Ex.PW1/6- Disability Certificate Ex.PW1/7- DAR/ Charge Sheet He was cross examined by counsel for insurance company. 5(b) Petitioner Evidence was closed. Matter was then listed for respondent evidence. 5(c) Sh. Shobhit Aggarwal, Investigator of Bajaj Alliance Insurance Company examined as R3W1 who relied upon summoned record 6. Final Arguments: 6(a) Final Arguments were advanced by counsel for claimant as well as counsel for R-3/ Insurance Company. 6(b) Counsel for claimant argued that the accident happened MACT No. 1052/2028 Manoj Bhaskar Vs. Mukesh Kumar & Ors Page No. 4 of 21 solely on account of the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle as deposed by the eye witness/ injured examined on behalf of the claimant. She has further stated that there is no dispute about the involvement or identification of the offending vehicle Manoj Banshkar vs Mukesh Kumar on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7283474/ 3 and the driver thereof. She further stated that injured has suffered permanent disability on account of injuries sustained in the accident which has adversely affected his earning capacity. Written Submissions also filed on behalf of claimant. PW-1 / Injured Sh. Manoj Bhanskar affirmed in evidentiary affidavit Ex.PW1/A that he was seated on the ground of Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir, Shyam Colony, Sehatpur, MACT No. 1052/2028 . 5 of 21 Faridabad, Haryana, eating food under a tree shed, that all of a sudden a speeding and rashly driven Swift Dezire car bearing Reg. No. HR 55AB 9547 impacted him without blowing any horn and without giving any indicator, due to which he fell down and received multiple injuries. He deposed that the spot where he was seated was not connected with road and thus was not meant for vehicular movement. Upon cross examination by counsel for insurance company, he stated that they were 7 to 8 persons present at the time of accident but only he had received the injuries. He clarified that the offending vehicle was coming from nearby bridge. He also clarified the accident took place in the afternoon while there was no traffic on the road and that he had not seen any other vehicle or heard any sound of plying of vehicle as he was sitting alone in an open field having lunch under a tree near Panchmukhi Hanuman Temple at Faridabad. He stated that he had noted down the colour of the vehicle was white and the driver was the only one present in the vehicle at the time of accident. He also stated that he has never sen the driver and therefore, would not be able to recognize him and that he came to know about the driver having fled away from the spot from the labourers present at the spot who rushed him to the hospital. He also clarified that the PCR vehicle did not arrive at spot and someone from the public had informed the police. He also stated that the driver had left the offending vehicle at the spot which was seized by the police officials from the spot, however, he was never taken to the spot of accident by the police. He declined the suggestion that any accident had not taken place due to involvement of alleged offending vehicle or that the respondents have been falsely implicated in this case. Mukesh Kumar & Ors Page No. 6 of 21 7(b) At the outset, it is noted that reply was filed by R-1 as driver of the offending vehicle who has nowhere denied the happening of the accident with the offending vehicle. There is no denial either that he was behind the wheels at the time of accident. He has chosen not to cross examine PW1/ injured to testify about speedy and reckless driving on the part of R-1/ driver being the sole cause of the accident. 7(c) FIR was registered on 06.06.2018 while the accident took place on 04.06.2018. It is mentioned in the FIR itself that a telephonic information was received in the PS with respect to a motorist having hit a person in pursuance to which HC Ramesh Kumar Ct. Giriraj proceeded to the open ground abutting Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir, Shyam Colony where they found Swift Dezire Car bearing No. HR 55 AB 9547 with lot of public persons having gathered at the spot. It was informed that the injured has already been rushed to the hospital while driver of the offending vehicle fled away from the spot. It is mentioned in the FIR itself that the vehicle was seized from the spot by the police officials. It is also mentioned therein that the statement of injured could not be recorded on the same date, being certified unfit for statement by the treating doctors.

Delineating the damages as pecuniary and non pecuniary, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case of R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt Ltd, 1995 AIR 755, made following observations: "9....while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages. Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which are capable of being calculated in terms of money; whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations. In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit up to the date of trial; (iii) other material loss. So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e., on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, hardship, discomfort, disappointment, frustration and mental stress in life." Certain principles for delineating just compensation were enumerated in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Following observations are relevant in the context: "40.General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 5. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. [See C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR 1970 SC 376] , R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. [(1995) 1 SCC 551 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 250] and Baker v. Willoughby [1970 AC 467 : (1970) 2 WLR 50 : (1969) 3 All ER 1528 (HL)] .] 6. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. MACT No. 1052/2028 Manoj Bhaskar Vs. In view of the above discussion of law, the calculation MACT No. 1052/2028 Manoj Bhaskar Vs. Mukesh Kumar & Ors Page No. 16 of 21 under future loss of income in the present case is as under: (i) Annual income (Rs.849712) = Rs.1,01,964/- (ii) Future prospect (40% of Rs.3,86,388/-) = Rs.40,786/- __________________ (iii) Total = Rs. 1,42,750/- (iv) Thus, Multiplicand = Rs. 1,42,750/- (v) Hence, the 'Total Loss of Future Income' shall be :- (vi) Percentage of Functional Disability (Multiplicand X Multiplier). 5% (Rs. 1,42,750/- X 16) = Rs.1,14,200/- Manoj Banshkar vs Mukesh Kumar on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7283474/ 11 19. (Reliance placed upon National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Yad Ram MAC APP 526/2018 also referred and relied in case of The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Sohan Lal & Ors. MAC APP 70/2024 of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court). Insurance Company has conceded valid and effective Insurance Policy on the date of accident and has not raised any statutory defence.
